{{Short description|Method for constructing models of set theory}}
In the mathematical discipline of [[set theory]], '''iterated forcing''' is a method for constructing [[model (logic)|model]]s of set theory by repeating Cohen's forcing method a transfinite number of times. Iterated forcing was introduced by {{harvs|txt|last1=Solovay|last2=Tennenbaum|year=1971}} in their construction of a model of set theory with no [[Suslin tree]]. They also showed that iterated forcing can construct models where [[Martin's axiom]] holds and the [[Continuum (set theory)|continuum]] is any given [[regular cardinal]].

In iterated forcing, one has a transfinite sequence ''P''<sub>''α''</sub> of forcing notions indexed by some [[ordinal number|ordinal]]s ''α'', which give a family of [[Boolean-valued model]]s ''V''<sup>''P''<sub>''α''</sub></sup>. If ''α''+1 is a successor ordinal then  ''P''<sub>''α''+1</sub> is often constructed from ''P''<sub>''α''</sub> using a forcing notion in ''V''<sup>''P''<sub>''α''</sub></sup>, while if ''α'' is a limit ordinal then ''P''<sub>''α''</sub> is often constructed as some sort of limit (such as the [[direct limit]]) of the ''P''<sub>''β''</sub> for ''β''<''α''.

A key consideration is that, typically, it is necessary that <math>\omega_1</math> is not collapsed. This is often accomplished by the use of a preservation theorem such as:
* Finite support iteration of c.c.c. forcings (see [[countable chain condition]]) are c.c.c. and thus preserve <math>\omega_1</math>.
* Countable support iterations of proper forcings are proper (see [[Proper forcing axiom#The Fundamental Theorem of Proper Forcing|Fundamental Theorem of Proper Forcing]]) and thus preserve <math>\omega_1</math>.
* Revised countable support iterations of semi-proper forcings are semi-proper and thus preserve <math>\omega_1</math>.

Some non-semi-proper forcings, such as [[Namba forcing]], can be iterated with appropriate cardinal collapses while preserving <math>\omega_1</math> using methods developed by [[Saharon Shelah]].<ref>Shelah, S., Proper and Improper Forcing, Springer 1992</ref><ref>Schlindwein, Chaz, Shelah's work on non-semiproper iterations I, [[Archive for Mathematical Logic]] (47) 2008 pp. 579–606</ref><ref>Schlindwein, Chaz, Shelah's work on non-semiproper iterations II, [[Journal of Symbolic Logic]] (66) 2001, pp. 1865–1883</ref>
